header.account: A US criminal and traffic defense law firm
header.health_math: 0 fails and 5 warns across the 6 scored areas
header.roas_targets: No campaign has a target ROAS setting or uses value bidding, no ROAS target was given, and every conversion value is 0, so all 9 campaigns are judged on CPA.

scorecard.why: 10 keywords spent at least their target with no conversion ($370); $80 of it is brand, which is never paused. 4 keywords meet the pause rule and 4 more go to review.
All 5 counted conversion actions report no value, and no value per conversion was given, so profit and ROAS per keyword can't be worked out. CPA against target is used instead.

scorecard.key_number: 31% of scored spend on Quality Score 1-5
scorecard.why: Spend-weighted Quality Score is 6.3; 13% of keyword spend has no score yet. Expected CTR is the weak part (12 of the top 20). Average CPC was higher on QS 7-10 ($8) than on QS 1-5 ($7), so no per-point penalty is claimed.

scorecard.key_number: 11% of search-term spend split across ad groups
scorecard.why: Phrase match carries 74% of keyword spend and there are no broad keywords. Close variants took 51% of visible search-term spend. 5 terms spent in two Traffic Tickets ad groups, and 1 routing miss. 5 steady phrase converters have no exact version yet (Migrate to Exact list).

One exact keyword sits in two Traffic Tickets ad groups in different word order. 2 more groups repeat between in-state and out-of-state campaigns, which exclude each other's locations: intentional. 29 redundant variants sit inside single ad groups.
4 ad groups take more than 25% of their search-term spend off theme. The biggest leaks are speeding-ticket searches in the wrong Traffic Tickets ad group and other people's and firms' names.
34 are already covered by a serving phrase keyword. Keyword Planner shows 10 of the 10 uncovered Pharmacy Board keywords checked at 0 monthly searches in the state.

top_actions.action: Fix Quality Score on converting keywords before anything else
top_actions.what: 18 converting keywords have Quality Score 1-5; 11 of them are in Criminal Defense, where expected CTR and ad relevance are both below average. Rewrite that ad group's ads in the searchers' words and split the city keywords out.
top_actions.evidence: keyword_view: 31% of scored spend sits on Quality Score 1-5; expected CTR is below average on 12 of the top 20 scored keywords, ad relevance on 4, landing page on 1.
top_actions.who: do this in Google Ads (quality-score-fixer can help, if installed)

top_actions.action: Set real targets for DUI, Criminal Defense and Nursing Board, then decide the review list
top_actions.what: 4 converting keywords cost at least twice their campaign's benchmark CPA, but those campaigns have no target CPA, so they are held for review rather than paused.
top_actions.evidence: keyword_view cost and conversions against each campaign's fallback benchmark; see review_list. 2 of them are also Quality Score victims.
top_actions.who: do this in Google Ads: set the target CPAs (bid-strategy-auditor can help, if installed); then rerun and I can pause what still fails

top_actions.action: Pause the keywords on the pause list
top_actions.what: 4 non-brand keywords spent at least twice their target with a CPA at least twice the target.
top_actions.evidence: keyword_view: see pause_list; each row shows the target and where it came from. 1 of them is also a Quality Score victim, so fixing its ads is the alternative.
top_actions.who: I can do this now: update_keywords with status PAUSED (payload below, not run)

top_actions.action: Fix ad group routing and exclude names
top_actions.what: Off-theme search terms took 13% of visible search-term spend. Speeding-ticket searches land in the 'traffic attorney' ad group instead of 'traffic ticket lawyer', and other people's and firms' names reach Criminal Defense, Traffic Tickets and Out-of-State DUI.
top_actions.evidence: search_term_view with segments.keyword: $20 on terms that fit another ad group, $90 on names of competitors or other people, $20 on related services with no keyword, $10 unrelated.
top_actions.who: I can do this now: exact negatives with add_negative_keywords (not run); I ask before excluding related services

top_actions.action: Stop Traffic Tickets ad groups bidding against each other
top_actions.what: 5 search terms spent in two ad groups of the same campaign, and the search 'traffic attorney' was won by a different exact keyword although an identical exact keyword exists.
top_actions.evidence: search_term_view: cannibalised terms carry 11% of visible search-term spend; routing miss on 1 term ($30).
top_actions.who: I can do this now: exact negatives with add_negative_keywords that send each term to one ad group (not run)

top_actions.action: Remove the duplicate exact keyword in Traffic Tickets
top_actions.what: 'traffic lawyer [state]' (ad group 'traffic ticket lawyer') and '[state] traffic lawyer' (ad group '[state] traffic lawyer') are the same exact keyword to Google, in two ad groups of the same campaign. Keep 'traffic lawyer [state]', which has 1 conversion at a $13 CPA, and pause '[state] traffic lawyer', which has 0 conversions on $30. One conversion is thin evidence, so recheck next month.
top_actions.evidence: ad_group_criterion inventory, normalised for word order and plurals; conversions and CPA from keyword_view.
top_actions.who: I can do this now: update_keywords with status PAUSED on '[state] traffic lawyer' (not run)
